title: Adaptive admin utilities: runbooks-as-resilient-tasks and support automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a compact set of admin utilities and a runbooks-as-tasks framework to let oncall and support engineers execute safe, idempotent remediation flows from the Console or CLI.

Scope:
- Implement a task runner backed by our existing operator step executor (lightweight, evented).
- Define a canonical task manifest format (YAML/JSON) with typed inputs, preconditions, and compensation steps.
- Provide Console integration (one-click runbook execution with parameters + audit) and a CLI shim for scripted use.
- Wire in telemetry (trace + per-step metrics) and structured audit logs for compliance.

Non-goals for this ticket: full RBAC rewrite, built-in chaos testing harness, or long-term stateful workflow persistence (we will rely on ephemeral task execution and S3 snapshots).

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We prioritize safety and observability over raw flexibility: runbooks will default to read-only dry-run unless explicitly authorized.
- Chose evented step executor to keep host agent footprint small; this trades off longer end-to-end runtimes for lower operational complexity.
- To reduce blast radius, we will implement tiered capability flags: safe steps (read/inspect), guarded steps (write with approval), and privileged steps (requires vault/KMS approval).
acceptance_criteria: Task runner prototype that executes a 5-step example runbook (diagnose -> collect logs -> apply config -> validate -> rollback) end-to-end in staging.
Console action that launches a parameterized runbook and records structured audit (who, when, inputs, outcome) to our audit-log stream.
Per-step tracing visible in Grafana/Jaeger with latency and error rate metrics; at least one alert rule for repeated step failures.
Dry-run mode works and prevents any mutating API calls; guard flags are enforced for guarded and privileged steps.
Security review checklist completed and signed off by Security (or documented mitigation if full signoff pending).

2026-02-23 - Marco Lin: Initial prototype of step executor completed. It supports sequential steps, idempotency tokens, and a dry-run flag. Pushed branch eng-420999-proto. Benchmarking shows median step exec ~120ms for simple read calls.
2026-02-26 - Erin Cho (PM): Reviewed prototype. Request to add explicit audit fields (action_reason, ticket_ref) to manifest and console UI before exposing to support team.

2026-03-02 - Security (Rajesh K.): Performed preliminary triage. Security asked for KMS-backed approvals for privileged steps and a proof that audit logs are immutable for 90 days. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-04 - Marco Lin: Implemented audit stream writes to audit-log topic with sequence IDs. Added guard policy enforcement and 'approval_required' metadata for privileged steps. Created PR #142.

2026-03-06 - QA (Lena G.): Ran end-to-end on staging with sample runbooks. Found issue: rollback compensation didn't run when validation step errored with 504. Repro steps logged in PR comments. Assigned bug to Marco.

2026-03-08 - Marco Lin: Fixed compensation invocation race condition. Added 5 new unit tests and an integration test that simulates transient infra failures. Telemetry events now include step.outcome and step.duration_ms.

2026-03-10 - Ops SRE (Carlos M.): Enabled staging alert for repeated step failures (>3 within 10m). Observed one runbook loop causing repeated failures; added rate-limit to executor to prevent thundering retries.
